content.text:
I submitted index 8 (Sb fraction 0.468). At 0.94% it had the highest EQE of the five compositions I measured, which used the whole EQE budget. I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so the phase explanation below comes from the phase database and was never confirmed by diffraction.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 0.35 | 0.23 |
| 8 | 0.468 | **0.94** |
| 9 | 0.52 | 0.89 |
| 10 | 0.56 | 0.52 |
| 15 | 0.73 | 0.30 |

- **Why I aimed there:** AgSbO₃ is the only silver–antimony oxide listed near the middle of the line, at an Sb fraction of 0.5. It is a known photoanode material, and its band gap of about 2.6 eV is below the 2.7 eV illumination.
- **What the data show:** EQE peaks around that composition and falls off clearly on both sides.
- **What's unresolved:** EQE was still rising from 0.52 to 0.468, so the true peak may sit a little further toward the silver-rich side. Index 7 (Sb fraction 0.437) wasn't measured and could beat index 8. If there were budget left, it would be the next one to measure.
